profile.founded: 1999, Hyderabad, by the Kanumuri family; Dr K Ranga Raju is Chairman and K Krishnam Raju (Krishna Kanumuri) is MD & CEO
profile.listed: 18-Dec-2024 on NSE (SAILIFE) and BSE (544306); IPO price Rs549

profile.sites: Integrated R&D campus at Genome Valley, Hyderabad (a new 100,000 sq ft R&D facility opened in Q1FY27); 700 KL cGMP manufacturing at Bidar, Karnataka (Units IV and VI; 80 production trains, 0.25-12 KL reactors, HPAPI block); discovery biology lab in Greater Boston (US) and process R&D lab at Alderley Park, Manchester (UK); land acquired for a ~40-acre greenfield manufacturing site at Choutuppal near Hyderabad (~1,400 KL planned)
profile.approvals: USFDA and PMDA inspections cleared at R&D and manufacturing sites ('100% successful track record'), COFEPRIS; EMA audits; >30 PSCI audits in seven years
profile.customers: 300+ active customers across the US, UK, EU and Japan, including 19 of the top 25 pharma companies; average tenure of large-pharma relationships 11+ years; returning customers >90% of revenue in FY25 and FY26

fy26.newModalitiesPct: 4% of revenue in FY25-26 (peptides, ADC payloads, oligonucleotide amidites, lipids); ~Rs118 cr and ~7% in FY25 on HSIE's wider definition
fy26.src: ar26 (notes 27, 28, 31-34, 42; MD&A key ratios); q4ppt pp.8, 11, 32-33

commentary: Revenue +12% to Rs554 cr: CRO (discovery) +24-26%, CDMO +6%; CDMO 60% of revenue, CRO 40% (CFO, 7-Aug-2026).
'Over 90% pipeline visibility on FY27 targets'; production started for 3 of the 4 commercial molecules added last year; Sai is primary supplier on 'probably' two of the three (deck p.8; CFO).

33 active commercial molecules and 14 in late phase; six late-phase molecules added in 15 months, five of them through large-pharma FTE (dedicated team) engagements; one Phase III approval in FY26, two regulatory milestones in FY27 and one in Q2FY28 (CFO).

A pilot with a large pharma converted into a long-term, high-volume discovery chemistry partnership; ~65% of discovery customers buy integrated services; aims to move two large pharmas to integrated models this year; another large-pharma process-development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2 (CFO).

H2FY27 to be stronger than H1 as capacity goes live: the first 225 KL production block at Bidar (of 2 x 225 KL) in H2/Q3; total capacity ~1,150 KL by FY27; a discovery facility opened in Q1 is already sold out (CFO).
Medium-term guidance unchanged: 15-20% revenue growth a year over three to five years and a 28-30% EBITDA margin; 'guidance should be viewed over a longer time horizon' given lumpiness (CFO).

FY27 capex Rs1,100-1,300 cr 'still stands'; no FY28 guidance; peptide spend 'less than Rs300 crores' to 2028, when a commercial peptide plant at the greenfield site should be operational; clinical formulation (oral solids to Phase II) about six months away (CFO, CEO).

legal: Public Interest Litigation before the Karnataka High Court on environmental matters in the Kolhar Industrial Area, Bidar, served after Mar-2026; Sai is one of the respondents; preliminary stage, no adverse orders (AR26 note 50).
Contingent liabilities are small (excise and tax claims); capital commitments Rs353.6 cr at Mar-26 (AR26 note 43).

accounting.effect: FY26 includes a Rs34 cr partial reversal of a FY25 provision on an early intermediate for a commercial product (customer destocking, then renewed orders); the loss-allowance line swung from +Rs30.6 cr (FY25) to -Rs25.3 cr (FY26). It flattered FY26 EBITDA by ~1.2 points and depressed FY25.
Company EBITDA includes forex gains (Rs29.8 cr in FY26, Rs19.1 cr in FY25); Screener and GAM put them in other income and forecast none. Company FY26 margin 30.1% vs 28.9% on the Screener basis.
57% of FY26 contract revenue (Rs1,211 cr) is recognised over time (FTE and development contracts), creating contract assets; other current assets rose to Rs624 cr at Mar-26 from Rs487 cr.
Rs31.3 cr of FY26 'other operating revenue' is government incentives (Rs14.9 cr in FY25); incentive receivables were Rs37.1 cr at Mar-26 (T-IDEA Rs13.4 cr plus others Rs23.7 cr).
Lease liabilities of Rs194 cr (R&D campus); lease costs sit in depreciation (Rs47 cr) and interest (Rs23 cr), so EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116; Jefferies values Sai on pre-Ind AS EBITDA.
Small: -Rs9.0 cr in FY26 (labour-code gratuity and leave), -Rs1.8 cr in FY25; IPO costs went to securities premium; ESOP charge Rs2-3 cr a year.
